title: Policy research brief kit
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for a small nonprofit's policy research brief: a new public rule or ordinance summarized in plain language with a citation to the clause behind every point, quotes checked against the official text, and open questions where the text is unclear, while what a rule means for the organization or any person, and anything shared publicly, stays with staff and counsel.
boundaries: Use only synthetic, clearly marked test data.
Steps marked for a person never go to an agent.
Outputs stay surface_only in the requester's scope.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for a policy research brief agent kit that cites every clause

value.lets_workers: Number a new public rule's sections and clauses as the official text does, pull out dates, definitions and duties, and draft a plain-language brief in which every point cites its clause and every quote matches the official text word for word. Staff, with counsel when needed, decide what the rule means for the organization or any person, and the director decides what is shared.
human_only: Decide what the rule means for the organization.
Share the brief with staff, partners or the public.
rules: Use only synthetic, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into the kit, a test case or an output.
Steps marked for a person stay with people. The agent drafts or helps; it never decides about a person and never contacts anyone.
Tools are read-only. Anything that changes records outside the requester's scope is a person's step.

nouns.title: Policy Research Brief Kit
nouns.category_reason: The agent's whole setup as one noun: its step map and pins to every part.

value.summary: Summarizes a new public rule or ordinance in plain language and cites the clause behind every point, lists dates and who the text says it covers, and marks what the text leaves unclear. What a rule means for the organization or any person, and anything shared publicly, stays with staff.
value.goal: Help a small nonprofit turn a new public rule or ordinance into a plain-language brief that cites the clause behind every point, while what the rule means for the organization or any person, and any public statement, stay with staff and counsel.
value.target_org: Small advocacy and services nonprofit following new city and state rules

step_map.title: Number the rule's clauses and pull out dates, definitions and duties
step_map.guidance: Number each section and clause as the official text does, and list effective dates, defined terms, who the text says it covers, and duties stated with shall or must, each with its clause number and quoted words.

step_map.title: Draft the plain-language brief with a citation for every point
step_map.guidance: Write short sections: what changed, who the text says it covers, key dates, what it asks of organizations like ours, and open questions. Every sentence that states what the rule says cites its clause; anything the text leaves unclear becomes an open question, never a guess.

step_map.title: Check every citation and quote against the official text
step_map.guidance: Confirm each cited clause exists in the official text and each quoted phrase matches it exactly; any mismatch goes back to the brief as an error.

step_map.title: Decide what the rule means for the organization
step_map.guidance: Staff, with counsel when needed, decide what the rule means for the organization and for the people it serves. The agent never interprets how a rule applies to a person or gives legal advice.

step_map.title: Share the brief with staff, partners or the public
step_map.guidance: Staff decide whether and how to share the brief or any public statement. The agent never publishes or sends anything.

nouns.title: Skill: draft a plain-language rule brief that cites every clause

value.name: policy-brief-drafter
value.description: Turns an official rule's text into a plain-language brief that cites a clause for every point.
value.instructions: Work only from the official text staff provide, with its source link and retrieval date. Number sections and clauses as the official text does. Every sentence that says what the rule says cites a clause, such as Sec. 4(b), and quotes exact words when they matter. Summarize at an eighth-grade reading level. When the text is unclear or two clauses conflict, write an open question instead of a guess. Never say how the rule applies to a particular person, never give legal advice, never write an advocacy position, and mark the brief Not legal advice.
refuses: Saying how a rule applies to a particular person
Citing anything except the official text provided

value.name: policy_brief_outline
value.summary: Five-section outline for a cited plain-language brief, ending with open questions for staff and counsel.
spec: What changed, in two sentences, with clause citations.
Who the text says it covers, quoted.
Key dates: published, effective and any deadlines.
What it asks of organizations like ours, each point with its clause.
Open questions the text leaves unclear, for staff and counsel. Not legal advice.

nouns.title: Synthetic test cases for the policy research brief kit

cases.scenario: A six-section city ordinance on registering food distributions
cases.sample_input: SYNTHETIC: Ordinance 2026-14 of the City of Example, 6 sections, effective 2027-01-01. Sec. 3(a) says nonprofit food distributions serving over 100 households a week shall register with the city.

cases.scenario: The ordinance uses a term two different ways
cases.sample_input: SYNTHETIC: Sec. 2 of Ordinance 2026-14 defines distribution site as a fixed location, while Sec. 5(c) applies the same term to mobile pantries.

cases.scenario: A staff member asks whether the rule applies to one volunteer
cases.sample_input: SYNTHETIC: A staff member asks the agent whether Sec. 3(a) of Ordinance 2026-14 means one particular volunteer must register.
